The lower Syr Darya is in the Cliopatria shape from 1856 (89 of the 153 cells of the radius); the other 64 cells enter the shape only in 1864, so the keyframes of 1859-1863 are corrected to hold the radius.
1859: the Caucasian Imamate falls. TE row: '1859 | Alexander II of Russia | Caucasian Imamate | Caucasian Imamate | Caucasian War'; RE: 'the Caucasian War (1817-1864)'.

region.text: the area east of the Ussuri

ledger.note: 1860, 14 November: the Convention of Peking ends the condominium.

region.text: the land east of the Ussuri to the Pacific coast

ledger.note: 1860, 14 November: the Convention of Peking gives Russia Primorye. AM: 'all land north of the Amur and east of the Ussuri would be ceded to Russia', the Pacific coast to the Korean border; TE row '1860 | Alexander II of Russia | East of the Ussuri River | Qing Empire (China)'.

1861, September: Russia takes Yany-Kurgan. CA: 'In September 1861, Alexander Debu led an army from Fort Dzhulek to Yany-Kurgan'; 'Debu captured and destroyed Yany-Kurgan'. khanate-of-kokand.json /ledger/16 is the mirror (c3). The page says the fort was destroyed; that the land became Russian is the researcher's reading, hence c2. Region: the Kokand dossier's radius.

region.text: Pishpek and Tokmak in the Chu valley

ledger.note: 1862: Russia takes Tokmak. CA: 'Eight years later, in 1862, Russia took Tokmak.' (Pishpek is named in the same passage.) khanate-of-kokand.json /ledger/17 is the mirror (c2). The Cliopatria shape holds 4 of the 67 cells of this region until 1863 and all of them from 1864; the keyframes of 1862 and 1863 are corrected.
1864: Circassia falls, the end of the Caucasian War. TE row: '1864 | Alexander II of Russia | Circassia | Circassians | Caucasian War'; RE: 'the Caucasian War (1817-1864)'.
1864: Chernayev captures Aulie-Ata. CA: 'led 2500 men from Siberia, and captured Aulie-Ata' (the 1864 campaign). khanate-of-kokand.json /ledger/18 is the mirror (c3).

region.text: the Kokand land between the forts that the 1864 shape takes in (868 cells; Shymkent, 37 cells, is among them)

ledger.note: 1864: bridging. About 868 cells of the Cliopatria Khanate of Kokand shape of 1863 join the Russian shape in 1864 beyond the places dated on either side (Aulie-Ata, Hazrat-i-Turkestan, the Chu valley, the Syr Darya forts, Tashkent, Khujand, Jizzakh). CA dates no Russian capture of Chimkent (Shymkent): it says only that the town 'belonged to Kokand'. The year is the shape's.

region.text: the steppe and desert cells of the 1864 step outside Kokand's 1863 shape (1,782 cells)

ledger.note: 1864: bridging. 1,782 cells join the Russian shape in 1864 outside Kokand's 1863 shape (Kazakhstan 604, Uzbekistan 785, Turkmenistan 358, the rest elsewhere); 1,512 of them lie in the Khanate of Khiva's land that its 1864 shape gives up (Ustyurt, Aral steppe and Turkmen coast; khanate-of-khiva.json /ledger/17 records that loss to nobody at c1). CA is silent on these lines; CA says the Russians 'crossed the eastern Kazakh steppe' in 1847-1864.
1864, June: Veryovkin takes Hazrat-i-Turkestan. CA: 'In June 1864 Veryovkin took Hazrat-i-Turkestan from Kokand.' khanate-of-kokand.json /ledger/19 is the mirror (c3).

1865, 29 June: Chernayev takes Tashkent. CA: Chernayev's forces 'determined to risk a storm', and 'on the morning of the 29th a deputation of elders offered surrender'; RE: 'capturing Tashkent (1865)'.

1866: Russia takes Ura-Tepe and Jizzakh from Bukhara. CA: 'Then he moved west and took Ura-Tepe and Jizzakh from Bukhara' (the 1866 campaign; a footnote reads Ura-Tepe as 'Apparently Istaravshan', hence c2). emirate-of-bukhara.json /ledger/6 is the mirror (c3, Jizzakh admin1 and Istaravshan 60 km). TE (second page): '1866 | Alexander II of Russia | Uzbekistan | Emirate of Bukhara | Russian conquest of Bukhara'. The region was all of Uzbekistan inside the 1868 shape, which held Tashkent and Samarkand; narrowed after the review of 2026-10-31.
1866: Romanovsky takes Khujand. CA: 'Romanovsky turned east and took Khujand' (the 1866 campaign, no exact date). khanate-of-kokand.json /ledger/22 is the mirror (c2).

region.text: Alaska and the Aleutians, Russian America

ledger.note: 1867, 18 October: Russia hands Alaska to the United States at Sitka. AP: treaty signed 30 March 1867, ratified by the Senate on 9 April 1867, 'The transfer ceremony took place in Sitka on October 18, 1867'; US$7.2 million; 1,518,800 km2.
1868, May: Samarkand surrenders. CA: 'the city surrendered without resisting (May 1868)'; RE: 'Samarkand (1868)'.

region.text: the Emirate of Bukhara without Samarkand

ledger.note: 1868, 5 July: Bukhara becomes a Russian vassal. CA: 'a peace treaty was signed' on 5 July 1868; Bukhara lost Samarkand and became a vassal. Cliopatria folds the emirate into the Russian shape from 1868.

region.text: 1870: about 320 Arctic cells (Novaya Zemlya latitudes, lon 52-68 E, lat 71-77 N) appear (the region is the set of cells of the Cliopatria shapes named in the note)

ledger.note: 1870: about 320 Arctic cells (Novaya Zemlya latitudes, lon 52-68 E, lat 71-77 N) appear. TE is silent; bridging from the shape.

region.text: the Xinjiang border cells added in 1871 (lon 78-84 E, lat 41-45 N)

ledger.note: 1871: about 106 cells of Xinjiang enter the shape. CA is silent on 1871; bridging from the shape (probably the Ili valley, not verified).

1873: Russia takes North Turkmenistan from Khiva. TE row: '1873 | Alexander II of Russia | North Turkmenistan | Khanate of Khiva | Khivan campaign of 1873'. The region is the Turkmen part of Khiva's 1872 Cliopatria shape.

region.text: the Khanate of Khiva without its Turkmen part

ledger.note: 1873, 4 June: Khiva sues for peace and becomes a protectorate. CA: 'on 4 June, the Khan sued for peace'; 'The Khanate of Khiva became a Russian protectorate'; RE: 'Khiva (1873)'.
1876: Kokand is abolished. CA: 'In 1876, the Russians freely entered Kokand, the leaders of the rebels were executed, and the khanate was abolished'; the Ferghana valley became Fergana Oblast.

1877: Russia holds the whole of Sakhalin. TSP: the treaty 'was signed on 7 May 1875, and its ratifications exchanged at Tokyo on 22 August 1875'; 'The treaty itself went into effect in 1877'; Japan cedes 'the part of Sakhalin island it then owned', so 'Sakhalin island as a whole became Russian territory'. TE (second page) tables the exchange under 1875: '1875 | Alexander II of Russia | Sakhalin | Empire of Japan | border settlement with Japan'. Dated here to the year the treaty took effect, 1877, to agree with the Cliopatria shape (Sakhalin cells 166 to 314 in 1877) and with empire-of-japan.json /ledger/14-15 (1877, c3); 1875 is the signing. Cliopatria shows the northern half from 1857. Moved from 1875 after the review of 2026-10-31.

region.text: the Kuril islands Russia held, between Iturup and Kamchatka (15 cells of the 1876 shape)

ledger.note: 1877: Russia gives up the Kuril Islands. TSP: Russia ceded 'the group of the Kuril Islands owned by Russia (between Iturup island and the Kamchatka Peninsula)'; 'the entire Kuril archipelago Japanese territory'; signed 7 May 1875, in force 1877. TE carries the Kurils only on the map column of its 1875 Sakhalin row. empire-of-japan.json /ledger/15 is the mirror gain (1877, c3). Cliopatria drops the 15 Kuril cells from the Russian shape in 1877.

1878, 13 July: Romania cedes Southern Bessarabia. TB: the treaty 'was signed on 13 July 1878'; 'Despite the pleas of the Romanian delegates, Romania was forced to cede southern Bessarabia to the Russian Empire'; Romania 'received Dobruja, including the Danube Delta'. TE (second page) names the Ottoman Empire: '1878 | Alexander II of Russia | Regain of Southern Bessarabia | Ottoman Empire | Russo-Turkish War (1877-1878)'. That conflicts with this dossier's /ledger 1856 (the land went to Moldavia) and with ottoman-empire.json /ledger/199 (1878-07), which lists only Kars, Ardahan and Batum; the Berlin page is followed, at c2 because the two pages disagree. The Cliopatria row 'United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia' runs 1859-1916; no dossier existed for it on 2026-10-31 (eu-18).

1878: Russia takes Kars and Batum from the Ottomans. TE row: 'Kars Oblast and Batum Oblast | Kars and Batumi' (the row carries no year of its own; placed in 1878 with the Southern Bessarabia row). Month: TB (second page) says the treaty 'was signed on 13 July 1878' and that 'The regions of Ardahan and Kars were also ceded to Russia'; ottoman-empire.json /ledger/199 is dated 1878-07.

1881, May: the Transcaspian Oblast is annexed. CA: Skobelev took Geok Tepe by mine in December 1880 and 'the occupied area was annexed as the Transcaspian Oblast'. The Teke lands had no state; the 250 km radius is an approximation of 'the Karakum desert area around Ashgabat'.
1884, 16 March: Komarov occupies Merv. CA: 'On 16 March 1884, Komarov occupied Merv'; the Merv Tekes had no state.

region.text: the Xinjiang cells that leave the shape in 1885

ledger.note: 1885: the 1871 cells leave the shape (China -108 cells). Page silent; bridging from the shapes.

region.text: the Afghan fort and oasis of Panjdeh

ledger.note: 1885, 30 March (18 March Old Style): Russian troops attack and take Panjdeh. PI: 'On 30 (18) March 1885, Russians attacked the Afghans'; 'By 10 September, it was roughly agreed that Russia would keep Panjdeh, give up Zulfikar'. CA (second page): 'When they captured the Afghan fort of Panjdeh, Britain came close to threatening war.' emirate-of-afghanistan.json /ledger/16 is the mirror (1885-03, c3). Region: a 40 km radius at lon 62.3, lat 35.7 (that dossier's coordinate; the gazetteer has no 'Panjdeh'), not the whole of Mary Province, which also holds Merv (1884-03). Narrowed and dated after the review of 2026-10-31.

1895: Russia takes East Tajikistan. TE row: '1895 | Alexander III of Russia | East Tajikistan | sparsely populated | Exploration of the Pamir plateau'; CA: 'In 1895, their base was moved west to Khorog facing the Afghans'. Cliopatria's 1895 step is Arctic cells, not the Pamir.

region.text: 1895: about 119 Arctic cells (lon 136-151 E, lat 73-76 N) enter the shape (the region is the set of cells of the Cliopatria shapes named in the note)

ledger.note: 1895: about 119 Arctic cells (lon 136-151 E, lat 73-76 N) enter the shape. TE is silent; bridging.

region.text: Port Arthur and Dalian, the Kwantung lease

ledger.note: 1898, March: Russia leases the Kwantung peninsula. KL: Russia 'formally leased the region for 25 years from China'; its ships had entered Lushun in December 1897; Russia governed it as Russian Dalian (3,500 km2).
1900: Cliopatria draws Manchuria (3,814 cells) as Russian. Neither TP nor KL dates the occupation; TP records only the 'evacuation of Russian forces from Manchuria' in 1905; bridging from the shape.

1905, 5 September: Portsmouth gives southern Sakhalin to Japan. TP: Japan received 'the southern half of the island of Sakhalin (Karafuto)'; TE row: '1905 | Nicholas II of Russia | Loss of South Sakhalin | Empire of Japan | Russo-Japanese War'.
1905, 5 September: the Kwantung lease passes to Japan. TP: 'Russia also ceded its leases in southern Manchuria (containing Port Arthur and Talien) to Japan'.
1905, 5 September: Russian forces are to leave Manchuria. TP: the treaty included 'the evacuation of Russian forces from Manchuria'; the evacuation itself took time and is not dated on the page.

region.text: 1913: about 117 Arctic cells (lon 80-105 E, lat 78-81 N) enter the shape (the region is the set of cells of the Cliopatria shapes named in the note)

ledger.note: 1913: about 117 Arctic cells (lon 80-105 E, lat 78-81 N) enter the shape. RE is silent; bridging.
1914, 17 August: the Russian army invades East Prussia. EF: 'The first full-scale operation was invasion of East Prussia on 17 August 1914'.
1914: the invasion of East Prussia is defeated at Tannenberg. EF says the invasion was defeated at Tannenberg; the page gives no date for the battle, so no month is set.

1914, April: Tannu Uriankhai becomes a Russian protectorate. TU: 'In April 1914 Tannu Uriankhai was formally accepted as a protectorate of Russia'; RE: 'gained Tuva as a protectorate in 1914'. The counterpart is the Cliopatria 'Republic of Uryankhay' row (1912-1913).

1914, September: Russia wins the Battle of Galicia and begins the siege of Przemysl. EF: 'the Russians won the Battle of Galicia in September', 'the Russians controlling almost all of that region by the end of 1914'.

region.text: the northern Iranian cells that enter the shape in 1915 (354)

ledger.note: 1915: Cliopatria's shape takes in northern Iran. EF is silent on Persia; bridging from the shape, unpaired to the end of the empire. See the war 'Persian campaign (World War I)' (PC: Tabriz entered 30 January 1915, Hamadan taken in December 1915).
1915: the Russians are expelled from Poland. EF: 'By mid-1915, the Russians had been expelled from Russian Poland'; the page dates no city.

region.text: Lithuania, Courland, western Belarus and Volhynia, west of the end-1915 line

ledger.note: 1915: the line is stopped far to the east. EF: 'At the end of 1915 the German-Austrian advance was stopped on the line' Riga, Jakobstadt, Dunaburg, Baranovichi, Pinsk, Dubno and Tarnopol; Cliopatria draws the loss in 1916.

1915, May: the Gorlice-Tarnow Offensive reverses the Russian gains. EF: 'In May 1915 ... the Central Powers began the successful Gorlice-Tarnow Offensive in Galicia'; the page does not date the loss of Galicia itself.

region.text: the Turkish cells that enter the shape in 1916 (214)

ledger.note: 1916: Cliopatria's shape takes in eastern Turkey. EF is silent on the Caucasus front; bridging from the shape, unpaired to the end of the empire. See the war 'Caucasus campaign (World War I)' (CC: Erzurum 16 February 1916, Trabzon April 1916, Erzincan 2 July 1916).

1916: Russia claims Wrangel Island. Chukotka page: 'In 1916, the Russians officially claimed the uninhabited island'; the island 'was subject to claims by the United States and Canada' (Canadian settlement attempts of 1921 and 1923) until the Soviets took it in 1924. The keyframes of 1916 and 1917 draw the whole okrug, the island included. [fx-43 review]

region.text: the Russian Empire's land at its fall, carried by the Provisional Government

ledger.note: 1917, March: the empire falls. RE: the February Revolution (8-16 March 1917), 'mass unrest in Petrograd and army mutinies', 'the establishment of the Russian Provisional Government'; Nicholas II 'bequeathed the throne to Grand Duke Michael'. The republic is proclaimed on 14 September 1917 (infobox). Cliopatria's row ends in 1916 and the Russian Republic row starts in 1917.

wars.name: Great Northern War (closing stage)
wars.outcome: Sweden cedes the four provinces by the Treaty of Nystad, 10 September 1721.
wars.note: TE and RE name the war and the treaty but do not date its start; the years before the empire's proclamation are not covered by the pages opened, so the span is the treaty year.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1735-1739)

zones.text: Azov, captured in 1736 and demolished under the peace

wars.outcome: Treaty of Nis (3 October 1739): Russia keeps a demilitarised Azov and Zaporozhye and gives up its claims to Crimea and Moldavia.
wars.note: The infobox says 'Annexation of the Zaporizhian Sich and the Azov fortress'; the text says Russia 'kept nothing more than a demilitarized Azov and Zaporozhye'. Austria joined in 1737 and made a separate peace at Belgrade on 18 September 1739. The war page gives 31 May 1735 as the start (infobox).

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1741-1743)
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Abo (1743) gives Russia south-western Karelia.

wars.name: Seven Years' War (Russo-Prussian front)

zones.text: East Prussia, occupied by Russian troops

wars.outcome: Treaty of Saint Petersburg, 5 May 1762: Russia returns all lands occupied during the war, East Prussia named.
wars.note: The page gives only the 1762 treaty; the dates of the war and of the occupation were not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774)

zones.text: the land between the Dnieper and the Southern Bug

wars.outcome: Treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca, 21 July 1774: Russia gains the Dnieper-Bug land, Kerch and Azov; the Crimean Khanate is 'formally' independent and dependent on Russia in fact; the principalities are returned.

wars.name: Bar Confederation and First Partition of Poland
wars.outcome: The partition treaty is ratified on 22 September 1772; Russia receives 93,000 km2.
wars.note: PP: the Bar Confederation 'fought Russian forces from 1768 to 1772'.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1787-1792)
wars.outcome: Russia gains Yedisan (1792).
wars.note: Only the TE row was read; the war page was not opened (page budget).

wars.name: Russian invasion of the Commonwealth and Second Partition
wars.outcome: Treaty signed at the Grodno Sejm, 23 January 1793, without Austria.

wars.name: Kosciuszko Uprising
wars.outcome: The uprising is crushed by Russian forces; the Third Partition treaty is signed on 24 October 1795; Russia takes 120,000 km2 with Vilnius.

wars.name: Russo-Persian War (1804-1813)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Gulistan: Persia cedes Georgia, Southern Dagestan and most of Azerbaijan, recognises Russian possession of the khanates.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Bucharest, 28 May 1812: Russia keeps Bessarabia and returns the other occupied lands.
wars.note: RT2 lists Revolutionary Serbia among the belligerents.

wars.name: Finnish War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Fredrikshamn, 17 September 1809: Finland becomes an autonomous grand duchy under the emperor.
wars.note: The years of fighting are not on the pages opened; the span is the treaty year.

wars.name: Napoleonic Wars (Russian gains)
wars.outcome: Bialystok from Prussia (1807), Tarnopol from Austria (1809, lost 1815), the Duchy of Warsaw occupied (1813) and given to Russia as Congress Poland (1815).
wars.note: The invasion of 1812 is not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Russo-Persian War (1826-1828)

zones.text: Armenia, the rest of northern Azerbaijan, Iğdir
Tabriz and Ardabil, occupied October 1827 to February 1828

wars.outcome: Treaty of Turkmenchay (1828): Russia gains Armenia, the rest of northern Azerbaijan and Igdir; Tabriz surrendered on 24 October 1827 and Ardabil was taken on 25 January 1828.
wars.note: RP2 gives 8 July 1826 as the start (Bash Aparan) and the theatres Erivan, Nakhichevan, Karabakh, Ganja, Talysh and Lankaran, and Tabriz and Ardabil; the territorial terms are TE's 1828 row.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)

zones.text: the Balkan citadels Shumen, Varna and Silistra
the Caucasus front: Akhaltsikhe, Akhalkalaki and Kars
Anapa and Novorossiysk on the Black Sea coast

wars.outcome: Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829 on the page, which also gives 2 September): Russia keeps Anapa and Poti, Atskhur, Akhalkalaki and Akhaltsikhe and gains the mouth of the Danube; Ardahan is returned.
wars.note: RT3: Russia declared war on 26 April 1828; 'Moldavia and Wallachia remained Russian protectorates until the Crimean War' - the page gives no evacuation date, so the 1834 end of the occupation events above rests on the Cliopatria shape only.

wars.name: Caucasian War (1817-1864)
wars.outcome: The Imamate falls in 1859 and Circassia in 1864 (TE).

wars.name: Crimean War (end)

zones.text: Southern Bessarabia and the Danube Delta

wars.outcome: Russia loses the Danube Delta and Southern Bessarabia.
wars.note: Only TE's 1856 row was read; the years of the war are not on the pages opened and the Ottoman Empire is the researcher's addition as a belligerent.

wars.name: Russian conquest of Central Asia
wars.outcome: Ak-Mechet 1853, Tashkent 1865, Samarkand and the Bukhara treaty 1868, Khiva 1873, Kokand 1876, the Transcaspian Oblast 1881, Merv 1884, Panjdeh 1885.

wars.name: Amur Annexation
wars.outcome: Treaty of Aigun (1858) and Convention of Peking (14 November 1860).
wars.note: No fighting between the two powers is described on the page.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1877-1878)
wars.outcome: Russia gains Kars and Batum oblasts and regains Southern Bessarabia.

wars.name: Russo-Japanese War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Portsmouth, 5 September 1905: Russia cedes its Liaodong leases and southern Sakhalin and evacuates Manchuria.

wars.name: World War I, Eastern Front
wars.outcome: Russia holds most of Galicia from September 1914 to May 1915, is expelled from Poland by mid-1915 and stands on the Riga-Tarnopol line at the end of 1915; ceasefire 15 December 1917.
wars.note: The empire itself ends in March 1917.

wars.name: Caucasus campaign (World War I)

zones.text: north-eastern Anatolia: Erzurum, Erzincan, Trabzon and Bitlis

wars.outcome: Russian invasion from 1 November 1914; Erzurum falls on 16 February 1916, Trabzon in April 1916, Erzincan on 2 July 1916; the armistice of Erzincan of 5 December 1917 ends the fighting.
wars.note: CC: the campaign starts on 1 November 1914 (infobox 29 October). ottoman-empire.json /ledger/219 opens the contest in 1914-11 and /ledger/221 records the 1916 loss. The empire itself ends in March 1917.

wars.name: Persian campaign (World War I)

zones.text: north-western Iran: Tabriz, Hamadan and the Russian cells of 1915

wars.outcome: Chernozubov enters Tabriz on 30 January 1915; Hamadan falls in December 1915 and Kermanshah in February 1916; the Russian army disintegrates in 1917.
wars.note: PC runs December 1914 to 30 October 1918; its belligerents field is empty and it describes 'a series of military conflicts between the Ottoman Empire, British Empire and Russian Empire'; Persia was not a belligerent. Tabriz was occupied in 1909 and Urmia and Khoi in 1910 (qajar-dynasty.json), which this dossier does not carry.

certainty.note: The Baltic, Polish and Prussian frontiers are fixed by treaty from Nystad (1721) and the partitions (1772, 1793, 1795), the Ottoman frontier by Kucuk Kaynarca (1774), Jassy (1792), Bucharest (1812) and Adrianople (1829), the Persian by Gulistan (1813) and Turkmenchay (1828), and are sharp; the steppe, Siberian, Kazakh and Pacific frontiers are approximate.

The Chinese frontier by the Aigun and Peking treaties (1858, 1860) and Portsmouth (1905), the western frontier by treaty, the Afghan frontier demarcated 1885-1886 (CA). Soft within the era: the protectorates of Bukhara (1868) and Khiva (1873), the Manchurian occupation of 1900-1905 and the Arctic claims.
The front lines of the war move month by month; the Iranian and Turkish cells are occupation.

notes:
Written by research agent eu-17-a on 2026-10-31 from 14 opened pages (the budget for a 65-shape state). Cliopatria rows: one, 'Russian Empire' 1721..1916 (65 shapes); the empire is ended in March 1917 here (RE), so russian-empire_1917 is a new keyframe and the Russian Republic row (russian-republic) takes over.

Shapes that look wrong or early (all verdicts in keyframe_review): the Caspian provinces appear in 1727 and leave in 1738 (RE/TE: 1723, 1732 and 1735); the 1762 shape holds occupied East Prussia; the principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia are drawn as Russian in 1769-1774, 1791, 1807-1811, 1828-1833 and 1849-1855 (only Bessarabia was annexed, 1812); the Second and Third Partitions are drawn in 1792 and 1794 (PP: 23 January 1793 and 24 October 1795); the 1864 shape already holds Tashkent and most of Samarkand (CA: 1865 and 1868); Bukhara (from 1868) and Khiva (from 1873) are folded into the shape although they were protectorates, and the whole of Turkmenistan appears in 1873 (CA: 1881 and 1884); Manchuria 1900-1904 is occupation; Galicia 1915 is occupation.

Cells that toggle in 1757-1761 and 1796-1858 cluster at Ladoga, Onega and Baikal (analysis of the shapes): lake-interior holes, not land.

Colonies drawn inside the Cliopatria shape and covered by their own dossiers (russian-america 1784-1867, grand-duchy-of-finland 1809-1917, congress-poland 1815-1915, russian-turkestan 1867-1918): this dossier keeps the territorial ledger (gain, loss) and does not remove them from the keyframes; the compiler should draw them in the colony tint of the empire. Alaska's mainland enters the Cliopatria shape only in 1846 although TE and AP date Russian America to 1799.

Not settled, for the gap-fillers: (1) the war pages for 1787-1792, 1828-1829, the Crimean War, 1877-1878 and the November Uprising of 1830-1831 were not opened (page budget), so the occupations of the principalities in 1791, 1828-1834 and 1849-1856, the 'Poles' row 1830-1833 and the Kars/Batum lines rest on TE rows or on the shapes at confidence 1-2; (2) the 1796 expedition (Azerbaijan, Dagestan), the 1812 French occupation of Lithuania and Belarus, the Ili cells of 1871-1885, the Iranian cells of 1915 and the Turkish cells of 1916 are in the shapes but on no opened page (confidence 1); (3) the Russian occupation of East Prussia 1758-1762: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_occupation_of_East_Prussia and the same title with '_(1758-1762)' did not load (url_not_found); the Treaty of Saint Petersburg page gives only the 1762 end; (4) the vassalage of Mingrelia (RP map: 1803), Imereti and Guria (1810) and Abkhazia is for the eu-19 dossiers; no ledger event was written for the principalities there; (5) Sakhalin: Cliopatria draws the northern half from 1857 but TE dates Russian Sakhalin to 1875; the 1857-1874 span rests on no opened page; (6) the Kazakh steppe: the vassal events of 1731 rest on CA's oaths, but the khans kept their power until the reforms of 1822-1824 (CA), so Cliopatria's Kazakh Khanate row to 1847 and the Russian shape from 1848 are both approximate; (7) rulers are omitted: the pages opened name only Peter I, Anna, Elizabeth, Catherine II, Alexander I, Nicholas I, Alexander II, Alexander III and Nicholas II, which is not a documented list; a gap-filler should open 'List of Russian monarchs'; (8) the Danube Delta, Yedisan and Transcaspian Oblast have no gazetteer entry (Yedisan is used as a region name; the delta is a radius around Tulcea; the oblast a radius around Ashgabat); (9) infobox areas checked: 15.0 M km2 (1725) against 14.45 M, 22.8 M (1895) against 22.34 M, 22.5 M (1906) against 22.30 M, all within 5 percent.

Disagreements between pages: TE puts the loss of all six Caspian provinces in 1732, RE splits it between 1732 (Resht) and 1735 (Ganja); AM gives the Treaty of Aigun only the year 1858 while TE tables the Amur gain under 1858 with the Convention of Peking; TE's table row for Kars and Batum and for the Finnish gain carries no year of its own (1878 and 1809 are placed by position and by RE's date).

Counterparts that need dossiers or are only names: Circassians (Circassia, Caucasian War to 1864) and the Karabakh Khanate (to 1813) have no dossier; 'poles' is a Cliopatria row (1830-1833); the Persian Gilan, Mazandaran and Astarabad lands belong to safavid-dynasty and afsharid-iran.
